features.note: The same accepted plan reads in every one of the 27 states: front band (LOBBY/TICKETS, CONCESSIONS, CHECKPOINT), 4+4 numbered salas 1-L..8-S and the REAR SERVICE strip stay visible through the translucent engineering shell; no zone disappears when fault/hot overlays activate.

Large/medium/small family labels and distinct room widths/heights remain legible in engineering-section and complete-network views across all states; fault-uc100b's west-band red halos do not flatten the 2/4/2 family distinction, and the east families stay untouched as a control.

Marquee, lobby/tickets, concessions, kitchen and checkpoint keep their framed identity under engineering overlays; hot-kitchen correctly ignites a red halo and red device in the kitchen block (front band) while hot-sala3 leaves that band clean — the sequence stays purposeful per state.

14 TC300 labels, UC-A/B/C/D, UG67 and the router→internet→Niagara→PC/tablet/smartphone chain all terminate correctly. Selection (TC300-08) adds white rings at the exact chain nodes (TC300-08, UC100-B, router, clients) absent in eng-none; faults alter only canonical reachability: fault-tc300 reds TC300-08 with its drop grayed, fault-uc100b reds UC100-B and grays bus-B dependents while bus C stays green, fault-internet grays the external chain with a red internet node while RS-485 stays green and LoRaWAN stays blue. Weakness: the selected path's edges get no continuous over-stroke, so the end-to-end path must be traced node-ring to node-ring at network distance.

All 27 captures are deterministic and mutually coherent: mode Ingeniería active everywhere, the pressed fault/hot button matches the scene, the HUD status line matches the alarm count and Niagara delivery claim in every state (1/4/14 eventos; 'Niagara sigue recibiendo datos' for hot states), and t0/t30 pairs are two different frames of the same pool in es, net and ug67 views.

important_features.note: Devices stay real-scale and gain rings/labels instead of false enlargement; the ug67 preset resolves the gateway, antennas and UC labels at device scale.
Interaction overlays preserve the gated hierarchy: facade red signage, dim salas, emissive network media; fault reds and gray-outs stay readable without blooming into the architectural lighting.
Bus trunks, drops, junction cubes and the ethernet run remain attached and routed in all states; the only containment noise is the LoRaWAN wave ring passing through walls at large radii.

defects: Selection highlight is node-only: white ellipse rings mark TC300-08, UC100-B, router and clients, but the route edges (bus B trunk, LoRaWAN B link, ethernet run) receive no continuous brightening, so the 'one exact end-to-end path' must be inferred ring-to-ring, and the rings are small at complete-network distance.

In the ug67 preset the LoRaWAN wave ring at t30 expands to nearly fill the frame and passes through walls, partially occluding the UG67 body and the UC-B/UC-C/UC-D label area in the close-up that exists to prove the gateway.

Fault/hot zone halos are large translucent room volumes; from the engineering-section camera the sala-3 red volume visually washes across salas 1-2 as well, so single-zone attribution only locks in after finding the red-ringed TC300-08.

The Capas checkboxes 'Techo' and 'Paredes' remain checked in engineering states although the roof is hidden and walls are faded — the panel does not mirror actual layer visibility (no alarm contradiction, but a state-reflection gap).
In fault-internet (complete-network view) the red node sits between the INTERNET and NIAGARA labels; the label-object offset makes it momentarily ambiguous which chain element is red versus gray.
corrections: Add a continuous emissive over-stroke (brightened tint that keeps the base green/blue hue visible) along every edge of the selected path: TC300-08 drop → bus B trunk → UC100-B → LoRaWAN link B → UG67 → ethernet run → router → internet → Niagara.
Cap the wave-ring pool's maximum radius (or fade opacity proportionally to radius) so at tick 30 in the ug67 preset the gateway body, antennas and UC labels remain unoccluded.
Clamp each fault/hot zone halo volume to its room's bounds and reduce its through-wall bleed (e.g. depth-tested or lower opacity) so hot-sala-3 tints only sala 3 from the engineering-section camera.
Sync the Techo/Paredes checkbox states with the actual engineering-mode visibility whenever a state change hides the roof or fades walls.
Center the red fault emissive on the internet-cloud geometry directly under its INTERNET label in fault-internet so the red node reads unambiguously.
